skill.name: prism-skill
skill.description: Prism Skill helps analyze events, claims, and fragments with adaptive disciplines, fact-checking prompts, structured Markdown, and optional HTML reports.
skill.summary: Adaptive multidisciplinary analysis with source-aware structure and multilingual output.
skill.author: sevenwoood

security_audit.summary: Static findings were reviewed against the source context. The alerts are false positives from installation documentation, Markdown formatting, multilingual text entropy, and an SVG that embeds PNG image data; no prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or malicious behavior was found.

remediation.issue: Large embedded PNG data URI in the SVG banner triggers obfuscation and unrelated keyword signatures.
remediation.suggestion: Use a normal PNG asset reference or an optimized multiline SVG without embedded base64 image data.

remediation.issue: README installation examples reference hidden skill directories in user home folders.
remediation.suggestion: Label these as manual installation destinations and avoid implying automatic writes to hidden directories.

remediation.issue: Example reports include dated factual claims that may become stale.
remediation.suggestion: Mark examples as illustrative or include source dates that users can verify before reuse.

content.value_statement: Complex claims often need context, source checks, and clear structure. Prism turns events or fragments into balanced reports with tables, flowcharts, and follow-up questions.
actual_capabilities: Selects one to three relevant disciplines for a user question.
Checks whether the input has enough context and asks clarifying questions.
Produces Markdown tables, lists, and text flowcharts.
Generates self-contained interactive HTML reports when requested.
Uses source priority and ethics reference files for boundaries.
Adapts the response language to the user input.
limitations: Live fact verification depends on the host model and available browsing tools.
It does not replace medical, legal, financial, or other professional advice.
HTML reports are returned as text for the user to save and review.
Illustrative examples with current events should be checked before reuse.

use_cases.title: Assess News Claims
use_cases.description: Break a public claim into verifiable parts, source levels, uncertainty, and likely effects.

use_cases.title: Structure Strategy Questions
use_cases.description: Compare an event through economic, social, policy, and organizational lenses.

use_cases.title: Create Study Reports
use_cases.description: Turn broad classroom topics into readable summaries with tables and follow-up directions.

prompt_templates.title: Quick Analysis
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a clear first pass.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this event in simple terms. Identify the main actors, causes, effects, and one follow-up question: [paste event].

prompt_templates.title: Fact Check a Claim
prompt_templates.scenario: Check a factual statement before discussing impact.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether this claim is verifiable. Separate confirmed facts, uncertain points, and logical inference: [paste claim].

prompt_templates.title: Compare Disciplines
prompt_templates.scenario: Use several lenses for a complex topic.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this topic through economic, social, and ethical lenses. Use a table and a short causal flow: [paste topic].

prompt_templates.title: Build an HTML Briefing
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced report creation after an analysis exists.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use our current topic and create a self-contained interactive HTML report with collapsible sections, theme toggle, and copy button.

output_examples.input: Analyze how a central bank rate change affects ordinary households.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a concise briefing, a household impact table, source notes, uncertainty labels, and optional follow-up angles.

output_examples.input: Review a broad health topic from a medical angle without giving personal diagnosis.
output_examples.output: The skill explains common mechanisms, warning signs, general boundaries, and a reminder to consult qualified professionals.

output_examples.input: Convert the current analysis into an interactive report.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a single-page report structure with collapsible modules, light and dark modes, and copyable summary text.

best_practices: Provide the event, timeframe, location, and desired perspective when possible.
Ask for fact checking when the answer depends on current or disputed claims.
Use HTML export after the main analysis has enough context.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to invent sources, statistics, or real cases.
Do not use it for personal medical, legal, or investment decisions.
Do not treat illustrative examples as current verified data.

faq.question: What does Prism Skill do?
faq.answer: It analyzes events, claims, or fragments through relevant disciplines and returns structured reports.

faq.question: Does it browse the web?
faq.answer: The skill describes source priorities, but live browsing depends on the host environment and available tools.

faq.question: Can it create HTML reports?
faq.answer: Yes. When requested, it can return a self-contained interactive HTML report for the current topic.

faq.question: Which languages are supported?
faq.answer: It is designed to adapt to the user language, with examples for Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, and Spanish.

faq.question: Is it suitable for professional advice?
faq.answer: No. It can explain general context, but it should not replace qualified professional guidance.

faq.question: What input works best?
faq.answer: A short event description with actors, timing, location, and the analysis angle gives the best result.
